column4: Producer reference for the specified construction
column5: STEICO LVL X, pine and/or spruce, nominal 39 mm and 13 veneers, with three transverse veneers; uses the X thickness-at-least-27-mm mechanical column. Layer bonding and interior scarf joints use phenolic adhesive; top-surface scarf joints use melamine adhesive. The approximate production wood moisture of 9 percent is not assigned as mechanical or thermal test conditioning. Temperature, specimen moisture, pressure and covariance across property summaries are unstated. No substitution for other LVL products or lay-ups is authorized.

column4: Mechanical table: mean and fifth-percentile density
column5: Mean density and fifth-percentile characteristic density remain separate properties; the latter is not mass density.

column4: Mechanical table and load diagrams A-D
column5: Parallel/perpendicular refer to the top veneer grain. load-edgewise=1 selects edgewise loading and 0 flatwise. Mean and characteristic bending stiffness are separate. Edgewise characteristic bending strength refers to 300 mm depth; no size correction is applied. Missing performance is absent, not zero. A bending modulus does not define a full orthotropic tensor.

column4: Mechanical table and load diagrams E-I
column5: Parallel characteristic tensile strength refers to 3000 mm reference length. Compression and tension are separate roles. Footnotes 1 and 2 assign the R transverse-edgewise modulus to compression, whereas X transverse moduli describe bending; these roles must not be interchanged. Strength values require separate design factors before structural design use.

column4: Mechanical table and load diagrams J-M
column5: Edgewise and flatwise shear are distinct load cases. Published mean and characteristic moduli and characteristic strengths are retained separately. No missing perpendicular-edgewise shear modulus or Poisson ratio is inferred.

column4: Physical properties table: design thermal conductivity lambda-R
column5: This design-reference scalar has no stated test temperature, specimen moisture or heat-flow direction. It is not a measured local-conductivity curve or evidence for a heat-capacity value.

column4: Physical properties table: wet and dry vapor diffusion resistance factors
column5: source-vapor-method-wet=1 identifies wet and 0 dry. Numeric humidity endpoints, test temperature and direction are unstated; no interpolation between these method states is supplied.

column4: Physical properties table: dimensional change below fiber saturation
column5: The source reports percent dimension change per one percentage-point wood-moisture change. Percent divided by percent gives the stored dimensionless strain-per-moisture-fraction coefficient. dimensional-change-direction=1 is longitudinal, 2 in-plane transverse and 3 through thickness. Longitudinal and transverse entries cite DIN EN 1995-1-1/NA Table NA.7; thickness entries are internal producer tests. Applicability requires source-below-fiber-saturation=1; a numeric saturation threshold, moisture endpoints, conditioning and uncertainty are not supplied. These coefficients are not a calibrated drying model, thermal expansion or evidence for a numeric moisture validity range.
